name: diag_diamond_axe_v2
what: a diamond axe: a broad wedge-shaped head of faceted cyan diamond with teal shadows, white facet tips and one small sparkle, on a long handle wrapped in red-brown leather with gold cross-bands and a round gold pommel, a gold collar where head meets handle. The handle runs along the canvas diagonal from the bottom-left corner to the top-right; the axe head sits at the handle's top end and follows that diagonal: its cutting edge is a straight or gently curved line running perpendicular to the handle, from the upper left down to the lower right (along the canvas's other diagonal), never a vertical edge and never parallel to the canvas sides. Filling the canvas corner to corner The head is a broad, heavy wedge of faceted diamond, as wide as an iron axe's, flaring from the collar to a wide cutting edge; not a thin blade, not a hoe or a pickaxe. Keep 2 px of empty margin between the head and the right and top sides of the canvas, so the cutting edge never touches a canvas side and is never cut flat into a vertical line. Draw the cutting edge as a diagonal staircase of single pixels stepping from the upper left down to the lower right, at the same angle as the canvas's other diagonal; the facets run along that edge; no column of the edge is more than 2 px tall.
